tyler: FYI, CI perf alert for eu-west A10 cluster after yesterday's merge. P99 generation latency jumped ~2.5x on a couple of model routes.:warning:

maria: which merge? any failing CI job IDs?

tyler: merge 64b2f7e (kernelselector change) landed in release-1.3. Job: perf/e2e_latency#427 — baseline p99 ~180ms, after merge ~460ms.

kev: started a local bisect, narrowing to 64b2f7e -> changes to kernel selection heuristics + new tensor-core fastpath enable flag.

nina: posting profiler snapshot from canary in eu-west-1 (A10):
```
PROFILE SUMMARY:
- total tokens: 1.2M
- avg latency: 110ms -> 270ms
- p99: 180ms -> 460ms
TOP HEAP (GPU): kernel_selector.cpp:135 (28%), kv_cache.cpp:89 (22%), attention_kernels.cu (18%)
FLAME (gpu time): load_kv 35%, matmul_tconv 30%, kernel_dispatch 25%
```

maria: interesting that kv_cache shows up. kev, did the kernelselector change any KV cache codepaths?

kev: not directly, but the selector now prefers larger tile sizes and enforces persistent attention kernel on A10/L4 which increases per-request memory pressure. That seems likely to increase KV evictions under noisy neighbor memory contention.

tyler: we saw noisy-neighbor pattern on that cluster around the same time (other tenants spiking memory bandwidth). nvidia-smi dmon during the spike:
```
# gpu util, memory bandwidth (GB/s) rough:
GPU 0: util 97%, mem_bw 410 GB/s
GPU 1: util 66%, mem_bw 430 GB/s
```

sre-lin: those mem_bw numbers look high for A10 in our tenancy pattern. Could be co-tenanted MLC jobs. We saw cross-tenant jitter earlier today.

maria: action items: 1) run bisect to confirm commit, 2) reproduce with isolated jobs on A10, 3) try forcing kernel fallback to previous selector for canary to see impact.

kev: bisect result confirmed: 64b2f7e is the culprit (selector change). Reproduced on isolated node with synthetic replay — p99 spike replicable.

nina: quick mitigation: set env USE_TENSOR_CORE_PREFERRED=0 for the canary deploy. Canary results: p99 drops from 460ms -> 195ms (close to baseline). Bulk rollout remains blocked until fix.

tyler: ops: marking rollout as blocked in the console and notifying sales.

ci-bot: perf/e2e_latency#427 failed: p99 regression +20% threshold exceeded. See: https://ci.redwood/invocations/427

maria: root cause hypothesis: selector change increases kernel tile size which ups memory working set. On A10/L4 with noisy neighbor bandwidth pressure this causes KV cache thrashing (more GPU->CPU syncs), so network/PCIe and attention kernels are delaying. H100 in our lab didn't show the issue because H100 has larger L2 and memory BW.

kev: profiling evidence: when forcing previous kernel mapping, persistent attention path uses 30% less device memory, KV hits increase (cache hit rate +12%), and latency returns. Patch idea: add hardware-aware downranking — if mem_bw > threshold or small free_mem, prefer smaller tiles / previous kernels.

nina: raised PR with conditional selector + override flag and a regression test that replays noisy neighbor mem patterns in perf harness. PR: https://git.redwood/pulls/2128

maria: please include CI job that runs on emulated A10 mem-pressure nodes (we have a cheap sim in infra). If CI passes, we can un-block rollout and cherry-pick to release branch.

kev: noted. Also adding telemetry to kernel_selector: selected_path, tile_size, free_device_mem at selection time. That will help catch regressions automatically.

sre-lin: long term: consider auto-routing requests from eu-west A10 pool to h100 or to dedicated nodes when mem_bw anomaly detected. For now, we'll keep canary pinned to USE_TENSOR_CORE_PREFERRED=0 until PR lands.

tyler: status update: canary rollback applied at 1746604500. Observed canary p99 stabilized at ~190ms. Rolling freeze remains until PR merged + CI verified.

maria: follow-ups: - kev: finish PR + tests - infra: add A10 mem-pressure CI job - ops: keep rollout blocked and notify customers on impacted routes

kev: will push tests by EOD. thanks y'all :thumbsup:
